title: memory.mark_conflicted wired into brain.reason's existing memory_path= mechanism
goal: Close the named gap: memory_recall already reports a prior valid note every call, but nothing ever compared it against what THIS call found. Wire mark_conflicted so a genuine disagreement is recorded, not silently dropped.
method: Two reason() calls sharing one SQLite memory store: the second supplies the first's own source passage again plus a directly conflicting new one, checking the conflict is detected and recorded. A second pair of calls recalls the SAME fact twice (no disagreement), checking the mechanism stays silent. A third, memory_path-omitted baseline checks zero behavior change for every existing caller.
results_prose: Call 1 writes a verified note from P1 (30 days). Call 2 supplies P1 again plus a directly conflicting P2 (6 months) for the same ask: 'supported', with exactly 1 memory_conflict_detected trace step(s), and P1's own note flips to verification_status='conflicted' in the SQLite store. A second scenario recalling the SAME unchanged fact twice (no real disagreement) produces zero conflict steps and leaves every note 'verified' -- the mechanism does not fire on agreement. memory_path omitted entirely: zero behavior change, no memory_conflict_detected step possible.
conclusion: lab.common.memory.mark_conflicted -- present since 2026-11-11 with zero callers anywhere -- is now wired into lab.common.brain.reason's existing memory_path= lookup_fallback path. A genuine disagreement between a still-valid recalled note and a freshly extracted answer for the same ask is recorded on the older note, not silently dropped or silently overwritten; an ordinary repeated, agreeing recall is correctly left untouched.
scale_down: One fact, one conflicting fact, two calls -- a proof the detection/recording wiring works end to end, not a measurement of lab.common.nli.judge's own contradiction-detection precision at scale (already a known, documented limitation of the classical judge, unchanged by this wiring).
follow_ups: mark_conflicted records the conflict on the note but memory.recall's own hit shape does not yet surface a note's conflicts list back to the caller -- a later recall of a conflicted note still reports it the same way as any other valid hit, just with a DB-side verification_status='conflicted' a caller would have to query separately to see.
models_used: lab.common.nli.judge (classical, deterministic: token coverage + number/polarity checks) -- no generative or real pretrained model involved.
